---
title: "Explore the collection"
subtitle: "The whole Sjónabók corpus at a glance: where the patterns come from, what shapes they take and how they are built. Click a bar or a dot to open the matching patterns in the gallery."
toc: true
---

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
db = FileAttachment("patterns/patterns.json").json()
P = db.patterns
kinds = new Map([["border", "Border band"], ["edging", "Narrow edging"], ["rosette", "Rosette / star"], ["motif", "Motif"], ["vertical band", "Vertical band"]])
hi = ({domain: [...kinds.values()], range: ["#10099F", "#2DD2C0", "#d61f69", "#FAC55B", "#FFA05F"]})
rows = P.map(p => ({...p, type: kinds.get(p.kind), group: p.frieze ?? p.point ?? "none"}))
```

## Every pattern on two sheets

Bands and motifs are shown apart, each packed tightly. Each colour is one source, in order from the top, so the colour changes run across the sheet. Click a source to open its patterns in the gallery, or a sheet to see it full size.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sourceColors = {
  const m = new Map();
  for (const p of P) if (!m.has(p.source)) m.set(p.source, {label: p.source_label, color: p.color, n: 0});
  for (const p of P) m.get(p.source).n++;
  return m;
}
html`<ul class="source-legend">${[...sourceColors].map(([s, d]) =>
  html`<li><a href="index.html?source=${s}"><span class="swatch" style="background:${d.color}"></span>${d.label}</a></li>`)}</ul>`
```

## Sources and types

Each file name starts with the manuscript or museum number it was taken from. Borders (long bands) dominate most sources; rosettes and figurative motifs cluster in a few.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 110, height: 340, width,
  x: {label: "Patterns", grid: true},
  y: {label: null},
  color: {...hi, legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(rows, Plot.groupY({x: "count"}, {
      y: "source_label", fill: "type", sort: {y: "-x"},
      href: d => `index.html?source=${d.source}`, tip: true
    })),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

## Shape

Pattern width against height, after the empty margin is trimmed. Bands lie along the bottom, rosettes on the diagonal. Hover a dot for its name, click to open it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  height: 460, width, grid: true,
  x: {label: "Width (cells) →"},
  y: {label: "↑ Height (cells)"},
  color: {...hi, legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.line([[0, 0], [130, 130]], {stroke: "#ccc", strokeDasharray: "4 4"}),
    Plot.dot(rows, {
      x: "trim_width", y: "trim_height", fill: "type", r: 3.5, fillOpacity: 0.75,
      href: d => `index.html#${d.id}`,
      channels: {pattern: "id", source: "source_label", density: d => `${Math.round(d.density * 100)}%`},
      tip: {format: {x: true, y: true, fill: true}}
    })
  ]
})
```

## Symmetry

Symmetry is measured automatically: a mirror or turn counts when at least `{ojs} Math.round(db.tolerance * 100)`% of the cells match. Bands are classified into the seven **frieze groups**, using one repeat of the band. Motifs and rosettes get a **point group**: D4 is the eightfold symmetry of a square star, D1 a single mirror, C1 none.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bands = rows.filter(d => d.frieze)
motifs = rows.filter(d => d.point)
friezeNames = ({p1: "translation only", p11g: "glide reflection", p1m1: "vertical mirrors", p2: "half-turns", p2mg: "vertical mirrors + glide", p11m: "horizontal mirror", p2mm: "both mirrors"})
html`<div class="pair" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr)); gap: 2rem">
<div><h4>Bands: frieze groups (${bands.length})</h4>${
Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 170, height: 260, width: Math.min(width, 560),
  x: {label: "Patterns", grid: true}, y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(bands, Plot.groupY({x: "count"}, {
      y: d => `${d.frieze} · ${friezeNames[d.frieze]}`, fill: "#10099F", sort: {y: "-x"},
      href: d => `index.html?group=${d.frieze}`, tip: true
    })),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})}</div>
<div><h4>Motifs and rosettes: point groups (${motifs.length})</h4>${
Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 60, height: 260, width: Math.min(width, 560),
  x: {label: "Patterns", grid: true}, y: {label: null},
  color: {...hi, legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(motifs, Plot.groupY({x: "count"}, {
      y: "point", fill: "type", sort: {y: "-x"},
      href: d => `index.html?group=${d.point}`, tip: true
    })),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})}</div></div>`
```

## Repeats in the borders

How many cells wide one repeat of a border is. Short repeats are small running motifs; long repeats are large meanders. `{ojs} rows.filter(d => (d.kind === "border" || d.kind === "edging") && !d.period).length` bands have no clear repeat within their length.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  height: 260, width,
  x: {label: "Repeat width (cells) →"},
  y: {label: "↑ Bands", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectY(rows.filter(d => d.period), Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {x: "period", fill: "#2DD2C0", thresholds: 30, tip: true})),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

## Density and floats

Density is the share of filled cells. The longest float is the longest run of filled cells in one row, which matters when a chart is knitted on a machine (long floats snag).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div class="pair" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr)); gap: 2rem"><div>${
Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 110, height: 320, width: Math.min(width, 560),
  x: {label: "Density →", tickFormat: "%", grid: true}, y: {label: null},
  marks: [Plot.boxX(rows, {x: "density", y: "source_label", fill: "#F4B8CE", stroke: "#10099F"})]
})}</div><div>${
Plot.plot({
  height: 320, width: Math.min(width, 560), grid: true,
  x: {label: "Density →", tickFormat: "%"}, y: {label: "↑ Longest float (cells)"},
  color: {...hi},
  marks: [Plot.dot(rows, {x: "density", y: "float_fg", fill: "type", r: 3, fillOpacity: 0.7,
    href: d => `index.html#${d.id}`, channels: {pattern: "id"}, tip: true})]
})}</div></div>`
```

::: {.legend-note}
All measures come from `gallery/scripts/build_gallery.py`, which runs on every build. They describe the digitised charts and can be off where a chart was split or cleaned imperfectly.
:::
